test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 03 Jul, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.

Delivering that furniture to the tenth floor without the lift and an incline is __incredibly foolish and next to impossible. __

options.text: like nailing jelly to the tree
like a tree known by its fruits
as tight as the bark of the tree
like going between the bark and the tree

solution: The correct answer is **Option 1.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given word segment **"incredibly foolish and next to impossible" **means something that is extremely unwise and almost impossible to achieve. (अत्यंत मूर्खतापूर्ण और लगभग असंभव) • **Example:** Climbing Mount Everest without any training is **incredibly foolish and next to impossible.** • **"like nailing jelly to the tree"** is an idiom that means trying to do something that is very difficult or impossible. (ऐसा कार्य करने की कोशिश करना जो बहुत कठिन या असंभव हो) • **Example:** Trying to get the kids to sit still during the long lecture was** like nailing jelly to the tree**. Therefore, the correct answer is: ***like nailing jelly to the tree**.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **like a tree known by its fruits** (पेड़ को उसके फलों से पहचाना जाता है): This idiom means that you can judge the quality of something by its results or outcomes. • **Example:** A teacher's effectiveness can be seen in the success of their students, like a tree known by its fruits. • **as tight as the bark of the tree** (पेड़ की छाल की तरह कसा हुआ): This idiom means something that is very close or tight. • **Example:** The friends were as tight as the bark of the tree, never seen apart. • **like going between the bark and the tree** (छाल और पेड़ के बीच जाना): This idiom means to interfere in a close relationship. • **Example:** Trying to mediate between the two lifelong friends was like going between the bark and the tree. 41:Tb3b, The correct answer is: **Option 4**.
